title: Duke Ellington hires Scott the next day at the Kentucky Club
summary: Ellington calls Scott as soon as he is let go and Scott joins him at the Kentucky Club.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: I took and I didn't say nothing, but it looked like -- I just sunk. I came home, and the next morning I got a phone call. Who was it but Duke Ellington. How did he hear about it so soon? See how things travel?

It must have been told around that he was going to change and get Joe Smith. Well, he called me, and he says, Scottie, you're open, aren't you? Well, I was open. That's what the musicians say: Are you open, and if you're open, you're open for work. You're not playing. I said, yes, Duke. He said, well, I heard you're not working with Fletcher. He says, I'd like to have you come work with me.

I didn't have the chance to feel any remorse or anything, because I went right out of the pan into the fire, so to speak. I went with him like that, the next night in the Kentucky Club. He only had one trumpet, Bubba Marley. And he had about eight pieces there, with me.
